messages:
maya: Hey team, customer (acme-med) on our Private on-prem package is seeing intermittent outbound failures to our API. They get 502s and TLS errors from the runtime. No-internet mode with corporate egress proxy. Can someone triage?

sam: What do the logs show? Any curl output from the host/runtime?

maya: From their runtime logs: "error: TLS handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate". From a test host: "curl: (7) couldn't connect to host". They also ran DNS and `dig api.redwood.com` returns `0.0.0.0` (looks like a sinkhole). They claim the proxy is allowlisted.

jorge: Quick checklist: 1) HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars present on the app/container? 2) Is the proxy doing TLS intercept (re-signing certs) or NTLM auth? 3) Is DNS being rewritten by split-horizon/DLP?

maya: Env vars are set. Proxy re-signs with corporate CA per their comment.

natalie: If the proxy re-signs TLS, the runtime must trust the corporate CA. Otherwise TLS errors are expected. Ask them to install corp CA into the runtime/container trust store or test with `--cacert`.

sam: Can they run these repro steps from the runtime host?

```
# test direct via proxy
curl -v --proxy http://corp-proxy:8080 https://api.redwood.com
# test DNS explicitly
dig +short api.redwood.com @10.0.0.2
```

maya: They ran `dig` and got `0.0.0.0` back — looks like their DNS is sinkholing the FQDN. That explains the immediate connection failure (curl can't route) and then the TLS mismatch when proxy tries to MITM.

jorge: 0.0.0.0 typically indicates DLP/split-horizon blocks. Two remediation paths: 1) Have netops remove the sinkhole / allowlist `api.redwood.com`, or 2) make the runtime trust the corporate CA and ensure the proxy doesn't rewrite the host header/SNI.

natalie: Add to checklist: confirm proxy auth method (basic/NTLM/kerberos) — NTLM/kerb may require extra client config. Also ask them to include corp CA into `/etc/ssl/certs` and run `update-ca-certificates` inside the container if possible.

sam: If they can, run a packet capture and show upstream IPs: `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host <proxy-ip> and port 8080` and share PCAP. Also try: `curl --cacert /tmp/corp-ca.pem -v --proxy http://user:pass@corp-proxy:8080 https://api.redwood.com` to see cert chain.

maya: I've requested a packet capture and full proxy config from them. Escalating to netops. Creating internal ticket IN-2345. @netops-bot can you assign?

netops-bot: Noted. Ticket IN-2345 assigned to ramon-netops. ETA ~2 business hours.

maya: Customer will try adding the corp CA to their container truststore and ask netops to whitelist `api.redwood.com`. They also asked for our egress IPs in case they want to allow IPs instead of hostnames. Reminder: for Private deployments egress IPs are typically customer-managed; if hosted, we publish IPs. I shared the doc link to our Private egress guidance: https://redwood.ai/docs/private/egress

sam: On support ticket, recommend wording: "Please remove split-horizon DNS rewrite for `api.redwood.com` or add a pass-through rule for the Redwood API host, and add corporate CA to runtime truststore. If proxy requires NTLM/Kerberos, provide sample config for our runtime to authenticate." cc eng-infra if proxy config requires code changes.

jorge: If they cannot change proxy/DNS, alternative is to use Private Dedicated with customer-controlled egress appliance or set up a peer where traffic bypasses corporate interception. We can document options but that'll be a longer-term change.

maya: Thanks — I'll update IN-2345 when customer confirms. For now: action items: customer to add corp CA + attempt allowlist; netops to review sinkhole; support to keep ticket open. :thumbsup:

sam: Thanks all.

maya: Closing thread here for now; will reopen when we have capture or whitelist confirmation.
